messages:
josh: Heads-up — sketched a mid-term plan to smooth telemetry cost spikes caused by high-cardinality traces. Idea: adaptive cohort sampling keyed by route/heatmap + SLO-aware prioritization. Quick check?

maria: Interested. can you paste the rough flow and the main tradeoffs?

josh: Sure — high-level: 1) lightweight edge profiler extracts a route fingerprint + cheap metrics; 2) dynamic cohorter tags traces as hot/cold based on heatmap_score(route) and recent query weight; 3) hot cohort: full spans, late enrichment, full billing metadata; cold cohort: compact envelope, probabilistic dedupe, reduced enrichment. Thresholds adjust by current query pressure and SLO budget. Pseudocode: 
```
if heatmap_score(route) > HOT_THRESH:
  assign_cohort(trace, 'hot')
else:
  assign_cohort(trace, 'cold', sample_rate=adaptive())
```

devon: I like tying to heatmaps+SLO. Main ops concern: compact envelopes at edge could lose billing key propagation for aggregated queries — how do we ensure cost attribution still accurate?

josh: Plan: compact envelope still includes a minimal breadcrumb: billing_key (hashed), tenant_hint, uncertainty_flag. That small header survives compaction and lets the billing pipeline attribute aggregated cost with a confidence score. We also attach a provenance token so late enrichment can rehydrate when needed.

lina: Rollout/rollback question — if we flip this on, how do we detect regressions and rollback fast?

josh: Canary plan: enable for 1% of routes, measure three metrics over 1h windows: telemetry unit cost, query tail-latency for cold cohort, and billing attribution mismatch rate. If cost drops but mismatch > MISMATCH_THRESH or tail latency increases > 5%, auto-decrease hot thresholds. We can gate via feature-flag: curl -XPOST https://ops-api/flags/cohort_v1?enable=true&percent=1

maria: Also run a dry-run sim. I can anonymize a week of traces and run the cohorter offline to estimate cost savings vs attribution leakage. Quick job: spark job that outputs per-route delta and estimated attribution_uncertainty.

observability-bot: FYI — created issue #obs-987: "adaptive cohort sampling follow-up" with checklist: sim, edge-proto, compact-envelope schema, canary playbook.

devon: Performance note — dedupe at probabilistic level helps reduce storage but complicates query reconstruction. We should document expected error bounds and expose them in the Console for any route using compact envelopes.

josh: Agreed. We'll add a per-route "attr_confidence" field and surface it in the Console and in the billing exports so downstream teams can decide whether to use precise queries or rely on estimates.

maria: One more tradeoff: more logic at the edge increases SDK complexity and upgrade surface. If we can keep edge profiler tiny (single header compute + small table lookup) it's acceptable. Otherwise maybe push cohorting to an upstream proxy instead.

josh: Good point — implementation options: (A) SDK edge (fastest, less infra), (B) sidecar/proxy (centralized rollouts), (C) ingress-gateway (single place but adds latency). We'll prototype B first.

lina: OK — next steps?

josh: I'll: 1) update RFC with the cohort design and compact-envelope schema, 2) open a sim job request (maria will own), 3) draft canary playbook and feature-flag toggle, 4) prototype sidecar POC. Ping me on this thread for quick calls. :thumbsup:

maria: I'll start the sim tomorrow and add baseline numbers to the RFC.

devon: I'll sketch the Console UI fields for attr_confidence and add a widget for per-route cost_delta.

observability-bot: Reminder — weekly obs-architecture sync on Thu 10a. Add this to agenda? (yes/no)

josh: yes.

lina: thanks all — short and actionable.
